instruction: Pick up the key, hand it over to the other hand, insert it into the keyhole, then turn it.

frames.label: Goal: pick up the key, pass it to the other hand, put its blade into the keyhole, then turn it while it stays inserted. A handoff counts only when the key follows the receiving hand after the first hand lets go. For insertion, the blade must enter the opening rather than rest on the rim; turning the handle in the air does not finish the task. Progress: The key is still on the table; pickup, handoff, insertion and turning are all pending. The left hand is empty and can prepare to receive the round handle. Next: Move the left hand into the open space between the arms and turn it to approach the handle from the side. Why: Leaving the round handle accessible lets the right hand lift by the narrow shaft and the left hand take the handle without the two grippers competing for the same part.

frames.label: Goal: pick up the key, pass it to the other hand, put its blade into the keyhole, then turn it while it stays inserted. A handoff counts only when the key follows the receiving hand after the first hand lets go. For insertion, the blade must enter the opening rather than rest on the rim; turning the handle in the air does not finish the task. Progress: Nothing has been picked up yet. The left hand has moved inward, but its fingers still need to face the handle in a useful receiving posture; the right hand has not approached the key. Next: Bring the left hand slightly farther inward, turn its fingers to lie above and below the handle, and leave a gap between them. Why: An open receiving gap lets the round handle enter from the side. Closing this hand before the key arrives would leave no path for the handle.

Progress: The left fingers have closed around the round handle while the right hand still holds the shaft. Both hands are at the key, so the transfer still needs a release-and-lift check.
